224.t: Music in school and the free violin lessons
224.s: West Indian mothers wanted sons on violin; a door-to-door deal gave him a free violin and ten lessons.
224.q: It was since I can remember. I remember at the Dudley school, West Indian parents, especially the mothers, always wanted their sons to play violin it seems like. Like I said, the street that we lived on, we had some other people from different parts of the West Indies there. They would have a boy…

224.t: The violin teacher and weekly group lessons
224.s: A fat white teacher wanted the fees; Haynes alone of the brothers took lessons at his mother's wish, though he wanted drums.
224.q: No, I don’t remember his name, but he was a big fat white man. He had these coins in his pocket during the – when we’d be studying, he’d be shaking his – all I could hear is the money and all the kids playing out of tune. Got girls and boys. He says, “E, A, D.” He didn’t care if we hit the wrong…

428.t: Playing violin teas with pianist Billy Kyle
428.s: Before he took up bass, Hall played classical pieces at Sunday black-society teas with Billy Kyle, his first step away from classical music.
428.ch: Philadelphia bands and the Club Harlem
428.q: And we knew what band was coming into the theaters so we would create their hit songs when they came into town. And while -- oh, geez, I'm leaving out a very important factor. When I was a violinist, Billy Kyle was my accompanist. And we used to play social events, play all these (humming), you…

428.t: First violin lessons and the junior high school orchestra
428.s: He gets a violin at eight, is badly taught, gives up piano at about fourteen and changes to a better teacher at Shoemaker Junior High.
428.ch: Family, schooling and taking up bass
428.q: She began teaching me piano and -- but I wanted to be a violinist. So on my eighth birthday my parents bought me a violin and I had my first violin lesson when I was eight.

125.t: Taking up the violin at twelve and the Flint citywide orchestra
125.s: Inspired by a girl violinist in his father's choir, he got a violin and became second violin in a citywide orchestra in Flint, Michigan, but gave it up as too hard to master.
125.q: Yes, that would come into the period when I was 12 years old. That's when I actually remember starting to play music, although I could play when I was five or six years old. I was always pluncking on the piano. And I

125.t: Giving up the violin as limited for a black man; his schooling
125.s: He saw that a black violinist would be limited, chose piano, and credits his father with good schooling and the chance to attend college.
125.ch: Early listening, piano and adolescent conflict
125.q: Yes, it is, and unusual. So with -- it was through him that I really got interested in the piano, to really want to play it. I knew that the violin was not for me, and I might also add while I'm talking about this, it's very important. My initial reason for discarding the violin, and this is in my…

771.s: He says he began violin lessons at about 12.
771.q: Yes, I was about 12. About 12. About 12, yeah. About, oh, about four years I was gone. I was playing. Mm-hmm. I was, in fact, I was just fast, you know.

457.t: Starting violin at six with a French opera teacher
457.s: His family was not musical; he began violin at six with the assistant conductor of the French opera, studying six years.
457.q: My first instrument was violin, which was my major. I started on that when I was six. And I started with a French teacher who was assistant conductor of the French opera in New Orleans. What was his name? By the name of Francois Kakel. That's K-E-R-K-E-L. I studied with him six years.

270.t: Childhood, schooling and violin lessons with Dave Perkins
270.s: Born in Donaldsonville, moved to New Orleans, church and school, studied violin with Professor Dave Perkins.
270.q: No, I was born in the house of the house. Yeah. Half the band, just children born and all about half born in the audience. Uh-huh.

15.t: Violin teacher Toad Johnson and studying until he ran away
15.s: Howard says his father played all types of music; he studied violin with Toad Johnson until his first runaway at fourteen.
15.q: No, you tell them in a few minutes, but they're going to tear all the pieces. Huh, huh, huh, huh.

338.t: Violin family and after-hours clubs while at English High School
338.s: Lesberg's violinist brother and sister, studying violin and viola with Carl Barladen, and playing Boston restaurants and after-hours clubs through high school.
338.ch: Boston youth and learning the bass
338.q: Quite a bit, yeah, actually. My brother was a professional violinist. He was about — let me see, Dave would have been — oh he was about 13 or 14 years older than I am. He was born in Russia actually. I was born in Boston in 1920. And my sister also played the violin. And I also took the violin.…

459.t: Deciding on music at six: violin and the nun
459.s: Shiner studied violin at parochial school where a nun spotted his talent; at Eastman he took oboe and bass.
459.q: No I studied violin at a parochial school where the nun realized that I had some talent, so she arranged to have me excused from class one hour in the morning and one hour in the afternoon so I could go and practice.

226.t: Disliking the violin; ordinary boyhood sports
226.s: Music was always present but he found the violin awkward, like golf, and was not athletic.
226.q: Music was always a part of my life, in the sense that even – I think I even went back to trying to have some study of the violin, but never seriously enough to really get involved in that, because I just never liked the instrument. When I say I never liked it, I just didn’t like the technique of…

104.t: Violin lessons with Miss Jarvis instead of piano
104.s: Her mother insisted on violin because of her violin fingers; after her teacher Edith Jarvis died, a poor replacement ended the violin lessons while she still taught herself piano.
104.q: Oh no. You see they, they . . . I guess I’ve come to a point here where I have to talk about music, because I wasn’t . . . I was just playing by ear. I remember

70.t: Buying a violin and studying with Mark Snyder
70.s: At eleven or twelve he buys a violin with his lamp-lighting pay, gets lessons from a Cincinnati Symphony violinist and plays solos with the school orchestra.
70.ch: Childhood and first bands in Ohio
70.q: So then I didn't like that. So they started to having music in the schools, public schools, so I figured, I said, "Now I've got to have something to play." So I saw this violin in the arcade at home. $16. And I was at a job lighting gas lamps, so I bought --

452.t: Elementary school and fifty violin lessons on Saturdays
452.s: After elementary school near home, Cobb enters Phillis Wheatley High and takes a mail-order style deal of fifty violin lessons at a downtown Houston building, getting the violin free.
452.q: Well, let me tell you. I'll give you the rundown on that. I come out of elementary at the end of it and went into the 7th grade at Phyllis Wheatley High School in Houston. And, of course, as time grew for a couple of years there, they formed a band. I was interested in the band, but by the same…

383.t: Violin with Maclo Williams, Talladega, and the Tuskegee dance orchestra
383.s: He switched to violin after hearing orchestra director Williams, played viola at Talladega, but piano reading let him join the dance orchestra and start a professional path.
383.q: Oh, I don't know -- I lost interest a little bit in the piano when I heard the orchestra director, Maclo Williams, play the violin, as a young kid, you know -- I must have been about 10 or 11 then, and I suppose nothing would satisfy me but -- I asked my mother to get me a violin; I wanted to play…
